answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the island schedule in the thread ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the haven checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 130 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. That is 6 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
